question.question: Can a partial persistVote failure cause requestVote to grant a candidate whose last-log term is below the local last-log term, although that candidate had no prior successful vote persistence in the requested term?
question.importance: A stale-log candidate grant can weaken election log-freshness protection and potentially authorize a leader without retained history. The exploration establishes only receiver behavior under constructed inputs, not a competing leader or committed-history loss.
contexts: One successful vote-term write and one candidate-key Set error that leaves the old candidate unchanged
No disk corruption or rollback of successful writes

obligation.description: For a well-formed request from an eligible candidate with no prior successful vote persistence for that candidate in the requested term, requestVote must not grant when the candidate last-log term is lower than the receiver last-log term, including after a failed candidate-key vote write that left its old value intact.

scope.description: Local vote log-freshness protection after a successful vote-term write followed by one reported, no-overwrite candidate-key Set failure. Stable voter configuration; candidate request fields come from its actual local log.
assumptions: Successful StableStore writes persist and later reads return their values.
One candidate-key Set returns an error without changing the previous candidate; other storage operations succeed.
Non-Byzantine messages, unchanged IDs and addresses, no log rollback; selected RPC losses and storage-preserving restarts are permitted.
No earlier completed vote persistence for the stale candidate in the measured requested term.
excluded: Behavior of a backend whose failed write corrupts data or rolls back earlier successful writes.
Proof that a particular production StableStore backend exhibits this failure.
Execution of later conflicting log commitment, state-machine divergence or client data loss.
General requirement to recheck every legitimate duplicate vote.

grounding.derivation: RequestVoteRequest identifies LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm as safety inputs. requestVote explicitly rejects a candidate with an older last-log term on its new-vote path and describes persistence as for safety. Its early duplicate branch is justified only by an actual prior vote decision for the same candidate and term; an old candidate retained after a reported write error does not supply that decision. StableStore exposes separate error-returning operations and no transactional pair API. The implementation itself returns without granting on the candidate-write error and continues serving requests. The claim preserves that freshness responsibility under the narrow no-overwrite error premise; it neither treats the tested behavior as its own normative rule nor demands new checks on true duplicate votes.
grounding.applicability: One successful vote-term write and one no-write error from the candidate-key setter; later eligible candidate request with strictly older last-log term and no prior grant to that candidate in this term.
alternatives: The attempted fresh candidate vote is correctly rejected on the write error, but that does not authorize a subsequent stale grant through a mismatched stored pair.
Known-leader and term guards remain enabled; the same prior leader candidate initiates the failed newer-term request, which legitimately clears known-leader context.
